sources_note: Official names, descriptions and grades as published for PlayStation 5. Guide text written for this tracker, drawing on the public guides listed in each trophy's sources field, accessed 20 Nov 2026.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the Platinum and it unlocks on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing separate to hunt. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap in this app: finish the story first, protect the one missable meditation trophy along the way, then work through strands, activities, crime and collectibles until the 100 percent completion Gold is done. If one trophy is still greyed out, that trophy — not this one — is what you still need.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, from start to finish. It is the first thing the story asks you to do, it teaches the basic controls, and it cannot be skipped or failed permanently — if a section goes wrong you simply retry the checkpoint. The trophy pops when the mission complete screen appears, so every player who starts the campaign earns this one within the first session.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission that belongs to Chapter 1 and the trophy unlocks as the chapter closes. Nothing in this chapter branches in a way that can lock you out, so just follow the story markers. One caution that matters for a different trophy: Chapter 1 is also when the meditation spot at Jason's home is available for Positive Mental Attitude, so meditate there before you move on for good.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Complete all of the Chapter 2 story missions in order. Like the other chapter trophies this one is unmissable and needs no special choices, loadout or difficulty — story progress alone earns it. The name is shown exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included. Expect it to pop right after the chapter's final mission wraps up and the game moves you into Chapter 3.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Work through the Chapter 3 mission chain until the chapter ends. There are no optional objectives tied to this trophy and no way to skip past it, so steady story progress is the whole method. By this point the map and most activity types are opening up, but resist the completion grind until the story is finished — nothing in this chapter expires while you play it in order.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish the Chapter 4 story missions and the trophy is yours. It is a pure progression award: no collectibles, no medal targets and no choices to manage. If you are following the roadmap, this is a good moment to sweep up any stranger strands and meditation spots in the areas the chapter opens, because the endgame cleanup is shorter when each new region is tidied as you reach it.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission of the campaign. This Gold marks the end of the main narrative, after which the open world stays available for everything left on your checklist. Before you start the finale, finish the one missable task — the Chapter 1 meditation spot for Positive Mental Attitude — and make a backup save if the game offers one, so the post-story cleanup never has to start from a fresh playthrough.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Play the named story mission Breakfast Run through to its completion screen. It sits inside the main campaign chain, so you will reach it naturally by following story markers, and finishing it — on any approach the mission allows — is all the trophy asks. There is no extra condition hidden behind the short description: complete the mission, get the trophy.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, one of the campaign's set-piece missions. Follow the mission's own preparation and execution steps as the story presents them; the trophy only cares that the heist is finished, not how cleanly. Heist-style missions are also good practice for the free-roam robbery trophies later, so pay attention to how escapes and wanted levels behave while the game is teaching you.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play when it appears in the campaign chain. It is a straightforward progression trophy with no optional requirements attached. Because several story trophies share this pattern, the spoiler setting in this tracker hides their names and descriptions until earned — turn it on if you would rather discover missions like this one blind.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. As with the other named-mission Bronzes, reaching the mission through normal story progress and finishing it is the entire requirement. No medal, no time target, no choice to get right. If the mission gives you trouble, lowering your risk — better vehicle, full health and ammo before the marker — is worth more than any trick.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish the VCIA Takedown story mission. VCIA is the airport, and this mission is also useful background for Catch Me If You Can, the free-roam trophy about leaving VCIA in an unscheduled way — the layout you learn here helps there. For this trophy itself, though, you only need the mission complete screen; the trophy pops with story progression.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory, a named campaign mission. Play it when the story offers it and finish it on any approach — the trophy tracks completion only. Together with the chapter trophies and the other named-mission awards, it forms the story spine of the roadmap: earn all of them in one pass and only the open-world cleanup remains between you and the Platinum.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100 percent on the in-game completion checklist. This is the longest Gold and the real Platinum gate: it pulls in story, stranger strands, activities, hobbies, collectibles and exploration tracked by the game's own percentage screen. Work from that screen, not from memory — clear one category at a time, use the filters in this tracker to mirror its groups, and save the broad counters (stunts, vehicles, areas) for steady progress while you travel between bigger tasks. Expect this to take far longer than the story alone.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts spread across Leonida. Stunts are the game's marked jump and stunt locations; each one you land cleanly counts once, so the method is coverage, not repetition. Sweep them region by region as the story opens the map, bring a fast, durable vehicle, and expect some ramps to need a run-up or a specific approach speed. Keep a rough tally per region so the last thirty are a short sweep instead of a full-map search.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the game's 9 activity types at least once. You do not need to win or finish any of them for this trophy — starting each type once is enough — which makes it one of the cheapest Bronzes on the list. Use it as a tour: sample every activity icon the map offers, note which ones you enjoy, because several other trophies (races, fishing, arcade, drone events) ask you to go back and actually win those same activities later.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — PlayStation tracks 42 challenges in total. Learn one weapon class at a time: find the target rhythm, memorise where targets appear, and replay a challenge immediately while the pattern is fresh rather than moving on frustrated. Accuracy usually matters more than raw speed until the medal threshold is close. This Silver rewards patience; split it across several sessions and the golds come steadily.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. A finish is not enough — the trophy needs a win at each site — so learn a course with a practice run, then race it for real while the line is fresh. Drone handling rewards smooth, early turns over late heroics. Tick locations off region by region in this tracker so you always know which of the 14 are still outstanding.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word different matters: repeating one easy race twenty times does not count, so keep moving to new race markers once you have won at a location. Mix race types as you find them, use a vehicle suited to the class, and treat early losses as course learning. This pairs naturally with Top Fun and with exploring for The Goodtime State, since race markers are scattered across the whole map.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Find the fishing challenge, learn its scoring — usually the weight or number of catches inside the limit — and use the best tackle the game has given you by then. Fishing challenges are low-pressure compared with races, so attempt this once fishing is unlocked rather than saving it for the endgame. If you lose, you can retry straight away; only the win counts.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game at any arcade cabinet you find in the world. Pick the shortest or simplest cabinet game available, finish it fully rather than quitting mid-game, and the trophy pops. It pairs well with Master of None, which asks you to sample every activity type anyway — do this while you are doing that tour and two checklist lines close at once.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's stranger strand all the way to his final mission, listed in the research notes as Puff Puff Pass. Stranger strands unlock in stages as you meet the character and finish each earlier job, so if Andy has gone quiet, progress the story or other strands and check back. Finishing his last job earns the trophy and also counts toward the 8 strands needed for the Strangers & Freaks Silver.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's stranger strand, ending with his final mission. Work each of Kenton's jobs as they appear on the map; strands sometimes pause between stages, and story progress is the usual key that unlocks the next one. Completing the finale pops the trophy and adds one more finished strand toward Strangers & Freaks, which needs 8 of the 14 strands in the game.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's strand through to his final mission. Start his jobs when his marker appears, follow the strand to its end, and the trophy unlocks with the last job. As with every named-character Bronze, the individual strand trophy and the Strangers & Freaks count advance together, so prioritising full strands over scattered first jobs is the efficient way to play.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. There are 14 strands in total, so you can choose the eight you enjoy most — but the named strands for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each carry their own Bronze as well, making them the obvious first picks. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, not when it is started. Track finished strands, not started ones, in this checklist.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's stranger strand, including his final mission. Keep returning to Randy's markers as new stages unlock; if a stage seems missing, advance the main story and look again. The trophy pops when his last job ends, and the finished strand also moves your Strangers & Freaks total one step closer to eight.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's strand through his final mission. The pattern matches the other character Bronzes: meet Tyrone, clear each job in his chain as it unlocks, and finish the finale. Strand stages can be spaced out by story progress, so do not worry if Tyrone disappears for a while mid-strand — he returns. His completion also counts toward the 8 strands for Strangers & Freaks.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: MISSABLE — the one trophy in the list that guides consistently flag as missable. Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. The risk is a single spot at Jason's home that is tied to Chapter 1: use it while you are there early in the story, because returning later may no longer be possible. After that, treat the remaining spots as a collectible sweep — meditate whenever you pass a spot instead of saving all 18 for the end, and keep count in this tracker so the home spot is never the one you are missing.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Pick up Bret's request through his strand or marker, track the animal using the clues and hunting tools the game provides, and bring the hunt to its conclusion. Unique-animal hunts are one-off events rather than repeatable counters, so follow the hunt through once you start it. Finishing Bret's hunt earns the trophy directly.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets. Cards are found in the world and grouped into sets, so collecting at random is slow — focus on finishing one set at a time, sweeping an area thoroughly before moving on. Cards you pass during story missions are the expensive ones to backtrack for, so grab any card you see while travelling. Three completed sets, not a raw card total, is what the Silver counts.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK interaction at 100 different locations. This is a coverage counter: each new location counts once, so spread your attempts across the whole map instead of repeating one convenient spot. Do a few in every region you visit for other objectives and the hundred arrives without a dedicated grind. If you save it all for the end, it becomes a long tour — start early and it mostly completes itself.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's challenges — there are 80 in total, so you can leave the 30 you like least. Challenges sit behind everyday play: driving, combat, exploration and activities all feed different challenge lines. Check the challenge list early, notice which ones your normal play is already advancing, and deliberately finish the nearly-done ones first. Fifty completions is the target; you do not need them all.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner alongside you, reach a 4-star Wanted level, then lose it completely and escape. Deliberately build the wanted level in an area with good escape routes — alleys, tunnels, off-road cuts or a fast car waiting — then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. Doing it with your partner present is the condition players most often miss: check your companion is actually with you before you start the trouble.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, without your Wanted level dropping away in between. Pick three shops close together, plan the driving route before the first robbery, and move fast: the chain breaks if you fully escape between shops, so stay hot on purpose. A durable, quick car and a partner present for all three robberies are the two things to arrange before you start.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. A vehicle is discovered by encountering and registering it in the game's vehicle catalogue, so variety is everything: visit rich districts, docks, farms, airfields and highways, because each area spawns different traffic. Steal or enter unusual vehicles whenever you see one rather than driving past. This pairs with On the Spot — register suitable finds in the Scooter Bros app as you discover them.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single activation of Combat Focus. Set the moment up instead of hoping for it: find a group of at least five enemies, position yourself with clear sight lines to all of them, start Combat Focus with a full, accurate weapon equipped, and prioritise quick centre-mass shots over headshot attempts. If a attempt falls short, story firefights and gang operations give you plenty of grouped targets to try again.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: At VCIA, the airport, make an unscheduled departure — in plain terms, get airborne in a plane in a way the airport did not intend, rather than using a legitimate flight. Get onto the airfield, take an aircraft, and take off. Expect a wanted response, so line the plane up and commit once you start. The VCIA Takedown story mission teaches you the airport layout, which makes this much easier after that point in the story.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The jokey description points at the Rhino, the military tank: research guides describe this as stealing a military tank. Provoke or visit a military presence strong enough for armour to appear, take the tank, and get clear with it. Go in prepared — full health, a fast approach vehicle, and an escape direction chosen in advance — because everything around a tank is designed to stop exactly what you are doing. Surviving the theft is the trophy.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected at any point. Scout the store first: entrances, staff positions and the quietest way out. Move slowly, avoid alarms and witnesses, and leave the moment the take is secured rather than looting greedily. If you are spotted, the attempt is over for this trophy — walk away, let things cool down, and try the same store again cleanly. Stealth, not speed, is the skill being tested.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Vault robberies are the heavy end of the crime list: go in equipped, expect a serious wanted response, and have the escape planned before you start — vehicle, route and a place to lie low. Each vault only counts when you actually get away, so a brilliant robbery followed by an arrest is worth nothing. Five clean getaways earn the Silver.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape with the take. Armored trucks appear in free roam; when you spot one, disable it or force access to the cargo using the tools the game gives you, grab the money fast, and run before the response arrives. The escape is part of the requirement, so do not start the robbery in a dead end. One successful truck is all this Bronze needs.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — the official tracking counts 52 areas to uncover. An area registers when you actually visit it, so grey patches on the map are your to-do list. Work the map methodically: drive the coast roads, cross the interior, and visit islands and small settlements that main missions never touch. Combine the sweep with stunts, WAiNK locations and vehicle discoveries so one long road trip advances four counters at once.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang — there are 9 gangs, so this means nine robberies, one against every gang's operation. Keep a written tally by gang name in your notes or filter this tracker by kind to review your crime progress, because the game is clearer about a robbery succeeding than about which gangs you have already hit. The last gang is usually the one whose territory you visit least, so check the tally before assuming you are done.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: UNCONFIRMED — the precise trigger for this trophy had not been confirmed in the guides consulted when this tracker was written, so treat the steps here as reported, not proven. What is reported: the official description says to enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach, and early reports point to buying or drinking a cocktail at an Ocean Beach spot overlooking the water, likely early in the game. Try that first; if it does not pop, the exact bar, drink or story moment is still being pinned down by the guide community. Sources consulted 20 Nov 2026 are listed with this trophy.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: UNCONFIRMED — the exact requirement had not been fully confirmed in the guides consulted when this tracker was written. What is reported: the official description says to smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style, and early reports describe driving a car out through a showroom's glass front rather than using its door or a test-drive exit. Try a showroom vehicle and a direct exit through the glass; the specific showroom, vehicle or mission context is still being confirmed, so do not treat any single reported location as guaranteed. Sources consulted 20 Nov 2026 are listed with this trophy.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Head to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley named in the official description and complete its bowling objective there. Play the alley's game properly through to the end — the trophy is tied to this specific alley, not to bowling anywhere else on the map. If your first visit only unlocks casual play, finish a full game before leaving. It is a short, self-contained Bronze that fits neatly into an activities sweep alongside the arcade and fishing trophies.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The playful official wording hides a character-building task: research guides describe this as maxing out strength with both protagonists, Jason and Lucia. Train each character's strength through the game's strength-building activities — fighting, gym-style exercise and other physical work — until both are at maximum, not just your favourite. Switch characters deliberately for this one, because progress on Jason does nothing for Lucia's bar. The trophy pops when the second of the two reaches the top.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: This counter trophy tracks Criminal Profile actions — PlayStation tracks a total of 500. Everyday criminal play feeds it: robberies, escapes, takedowns and other profiled offences all move the number. You should not need a dedicated grind if you are doing the crime trophies anyway, but if it lags near the end, repeat quick, low-risk profile actions until the counter reaches 500. Check the tracked total rather than guessing from hours played.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: UNCONFIRMED — at the time the guides consulted for this tracker were written, the unlock method for this trophy was not known yet, and this entry will not invent one. What exists is only the official description, Second time's the charm, which hints at succeeding at something on a second attempt after a first failure. If you earn it accidentally, note exactly what failed and then succeeded — that detail is what the guide community is still looking for. Sources consulted 20 Nov 2026 are listed with this trophy, and none of them states a confirmed method.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: UNCONFIRMED — this is a hidden trophy and its unlock method had not been confirmed in the guides consulted when this tracker was written. The official description, What the hell just happened?, suggests witnessing a strange or unexplained event in the world, and early speculation points toward an odd encounter somewhere in Leonida, but no location or trigger is verified. Explore thoroughly, investigate unusual sights rather than driving past them, and treat any specific pin on a map with suspicion until a source confirms it. Sources consulted 20 Nov 2026 are listed with this trophy.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: UNCONFIRMED — the precise method for this trophy was still being confirmed in the guides consulted when this tracker was written. What is reported: the official description says to bowl someone over with a melee drive-by, which points to striking a pedestrian or enemy with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. The open questions are the details — how many targets, whether it must be one pass, and which vehicles or weapons qualify — so try a melee drive-by when a safe chance appears, but do not rely on any exact count until a source confirms it. Sources consulted 20 Nov 2026 are listed with this trophy.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder a total of $250,000 in Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and criminal work; instead of spending them raw, route them through the laundering contacts the game introduces and let the cumulative laundered total build. This is a money counter, not a single big score, so start laundering early and keep feeding bills through whenever you have them. Waiting until the end turns it into a farming session; steady play makes it free.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend a cumulative $100,000 across all shops. Every legitimate purchase counts — vehicles, weapons, clothing, services and upgrades — so normal play contributes constantly. Do not hoard cash out of habit: buy the gear the harder trophies need and this counter climbs on its own. If it is short near the end, expensive vehicle and property-adjacent purchases close the gap fastest. The total is across all shops combined, not in any single store.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 purchasable garage properties on the map. Garages cost serious money, so this trophy sits late in a normal playthrough: earn through story, robberies and laundering first, then buy the remaining garages in one property sweep. Each purchase also gives your vehicle collection somewhere to live, which supports the vehicle discovery trophies. Eight owned garages — not visited, owned — is the finish line.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles through the Scooter Bros app. When you find a vehicle worth keeping — especially an unusual one that also counts toward Whip It Good's 100 discoveries — register it in the app there and then instead of driving away. Ten registrations is a small target that is easy to forget, so make registration a habit from the first hours and this Bronze closes long before the endgame cleanup begins.
